title: Borrowed fmpz exact aggregates
objective: Extend the fail-closed resident-fmpz backend through nested internal helpers that borrow NativeIntegerVector, FmpzMatrix, and IntegerBuffer parameters, with no public aggregate ABI, no ownership transfer, and differential/generated-code proof of zero mpz conversion in the qualified closure

oracles: dynamic JavaScript, GMP exact backend, and fmpz backend differential execution
generated internal C contains no mpz calls or fmpz/mpz conversions

handoff.summary: Closed resident-fmpz programs may now pass caller-owned NativeIntegerVector, FmpzMatrix, and IntegerBuffer aggregates through nested internal helpers without repacking, ownership transfer, cleanup, or a public aggregate ABI. NativeIntegerVector parameters lower as borrowed fmpz-vector pointers, preserving the distinction between local address-taking and direct borrowed forwarding; matrix and packed-buffer arguments preserve direct aliasing. Selection remains atomic and fail closed. A nested differential witness covers two vectors, one matrix, packed buffers, visible mutation, negative and promoted integers, tuples, early failure/recovery, and structurally proves that qualified helper bodies contain no mpz bridge or fmpz/mpz conversion. The promoted path exposed a FLINT cached-wrapper lifetime hazard, fixed by draining exact TLS checkpoint caches before suspending and rewinding the arena for result publication. Focused tests pass 14/14, strict baselib passes with 0 errors, and a complete build passes. The architecture umbrella reached the optimizer-dashboard manifest check after all preceding checks passed, where integration must regenerate the shared unclaimed digest. The native umbrella passed its package suites and reached 79 pass / 1 skip in the combined host phase, then stopped at an unmodified FFI platform-link fixture whose missing link array raises in compiler.cjs.
risks: Execution evidence is Linux x64; the generated C ABI is platform-neutral, but required release platforms still need integration CI.
The shared optimizer-opportunity dashboard manifest must be regenerated after integration because exact-analysis changed.
The full native umbrella remains blocked by the unrelated native foreign-input platform-link fixture failure in test/ffi.cjs.
next_steps: Regenerate shared optimizer-opportunity artifacts in the integration lane and run the complete architecture/native matrix.
Extend fmpz vector indexing to accept exact Integer indices; the cubic audit found this is the next structural blocker in 28 functions (262 reads and 98 writes).
After exact-index support, re-audit the cubic closure and address the next smallest fail-closed obstruction rather than widening public aggregate ABI.
